records.text: At 8:02 p.m. on September 11, a retired detective told Nate Brooksby that he knew who Charlie Kirk's shooter was and was trying to get him to surrender voluntarily.
records.speaker: Nate Brooksby

appearances.snippet: At exactly 8.02 on the 11th, I received a call from a friend of mine who happens to be a retired detective that worked for me for many years. ... So he said, hey, I know who Charlie Kirk's shooter is. I know the family through religious association. ... And he's in Washington County now, and we're working on trying to get him to come in voluntarily.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous reporting of Sheriff Brooksby's press conference records that he said he received the call at exactly 8:02 p.m. from a retired detective who claimed to know the shooter and was working on voluntary surrender. Confidence is medium because this verifies Brooksby's first-person account, not an independently timestamped call record.

records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: He's describing Mike Mitchell. Mike Mitchell is not just his Boy Scout leader. He's not just the former police officer, undercover police officer, and all the evidence points to the fact that he did work undercover in sex crimes, which is a running theme in this story, but he is also a minister at the Mormon church.

verification.notes: The source appearance was reviewed at 00:33:04. Public records and reporting support that Mike Mitchell was a former Washington County deputy and family friend involved in arranging surrender; Trump separately described a law-enforcement-connected minister. A secondary report cites older press accounts of undercover child-predator investigations, but current reliable sources do not firmly establish that work or that Mitchell held a ministerial role in the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. The combined claim is therefore only partially supported.

records.text: Owens said Mike Mitchell recognized Tyler Robinson and 'got the ball rolling.'
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It was him that recognized Tyler Robinson and got the ball rolling, which I have been saying from the beginning.

verification.notes: The source appearance was reviewed at 00:33:22. Official charging information says Robinson's mother first thought the image looked like him and his father agreed; the family friend became involved later at the father's request and helped convince Robinson to surrender. Thus the claim that Mitchell 'got the ball rolling' is broadly supported as facilitation, but the more specific claim that Mitchell was the person who recognized Robinson is contradicted by the official account.
